reader.requirement: For an indexed file open with sequential access (OUTPUT or EXTEND, the only modes Table 2 allows WRITE in), each WRITE must release a prime key strictly greater, in the file's collating sequence (in 1985 the native one: there is no file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause and the program collating sequence covers only relations, condition-names, CONTROL and SORT/MERGE), than the previous record's; under EXTEND the first must exceed the highest key in the file; a violation is GR17a's invalid key condition (status 21).

edition-consulted.switches: Constructs.FileCollatingClause2002: the file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause is refused at 85 (accepted at 2023), so an 85 indexed file's key order is always the native one

DialectBehavior.FileSharingFacility: at 85 a clause-less OPEN gets FileSharing.AllOther (Table 19 not asked); at 2023 NoOther/ReadOnly. Reached at OPEN, not inside WRITE; a single connector's WRITE result is the same either way

reader.edition-search: grep -n 'Edition|DialectBehavior|DialectLevel|CobolVersion' over IndexedConnector.cs, KeyedConnector.cs, KeyedStore.cs, FileRegistry.cs, FileSupport.cs (only READ, CLOSE WITH LOCK and sharing sites; none in IndexedConnector#Write, #Opened, KeyedConnector#RecordWriteFailed); the same grep over KeyedIoEmitter.cs, SequentialIoEmitter.cs, EcEmitter.cs, DispatchEmitter.cs, UseTierEmitter.cs (DialectLevel only passed to registration, SELECT WHEN, EmitRunUseBody); KeyedIoBinder.cs uses ctx.Edition only as the diagnostic sink
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the runtime ascending check is edition-free; 2002 adds a file COLLATING SEQUENCE clause, refused at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f25_05 covers OUTPUT and EXTEND order under the native sequence; not exercised: an equal key, EXTEND on an empty file, a program collating sequence that differs from native, the FROM form

reader.notes: Write tests Access==Sequential and compares the prime with _lastWrittenPrime under the prime key order (ordinal unless a 2002 file clause or CODE-SET is present, both refused at 85); Opened seeds _lastWrittenPrime from the prime tree's last key under EXTEND. The probe shows a reversed program collating sequence governing IF but not the file's key order, as 1985 VI.4.4.4 GR7/GR8 require.

refuter.evidence: Read IndexedConnector#Write (line 699: _orders.Prime.Compare(prime, lastPrime) <= 0 -> '21'), #KeyBytes (FileCharacterSet.Medium, ISO-8859-1 under the storage-byte law), #KeyOrder (Ordinal when no collation and no CODE-SET), #Opened (EXTEND seeds the highest key). Probe r3hv.cob (run r3hv-001, --std 85): K1 = 'A' & FUNCTION CHAR(256) (U+00FF), K2 = 'A' & HIGH-VALUE (U+FFFF). 'IF K2 > K1' prints 'NATIVE: K2 > K1'; sequential OUTPUT WRITE K1 'SEQ W1 OK 00', then WRITE K2 'SEQ W2 IK 21' although K2 is strictly greater in the native sequence. Same at --std 2023 (r3hv23-002). Probe r1alt.cob (r1alt-001): EXTEND ascending check against the highest existing key, equal key -> 21 (B002DDDEEE). Native order stands for every other character: the 1985 rationale names the native collating sequence for indexed files. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:IX.4.9.4 GR14  (4.9.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR14'; 'OK  §1985:VI.4.4.4 GR6  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR6'.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Runtime/Values/Text/StorageByte.cs#StorageByte (the storage-byte law, edition-free): U+00FF and U+FFFF share the byte 0xFF, so the file key order folds two native characters into one
refuter.corrected: The verdict holds only under the reading that 'the collating sequence of the file' is the byte medium's, in which U+00FF and HIGH-VALUE are one character (DOC-A.1-31, owner R52's accepted cost). Under the reading that the file uses the native collating sequence of the 65,536-code-unit native set (DOC-A.1-31's own repertoire, and the 1985 rationale's 'native collating sequence'), a strictly ascending pair of prime keys is refused with 21: a wrong answer, cause (b), the same at 2023. No kb/Work note records the key consequence; PB1759 records the fold.
